subject.title: [Feature Request] Hook Chain Integrity Protection Against Message Tampering

question: What hook-chain security model should OpenClaw support for mutable plugin hooks: host-owned audit/provenance for current in-process plugins, integrity checks across a future isolated-plugin IPC boundary, or per-hook permission gating first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementing checksums, audit logs, or per-hook allowlists would encode plugin trust-boundary and compatibility policy that current source and docs do not settle.

options.title: Define audit and trust boundary first
options.body: Document the threat model, redaction and retention rules, and compatibility plan before changing hook runner behavior or config.

options.title: Ship redacted audit first
options.body: Add host-owned audit events for modifying hooks while deferring checksum enforcement and per-hook allowlists.

options.title: Defer checksums to isolated IPC
options.body: Keep checksum enforcement blocked on process-isolation work so integrity checks protect a real host/plugin boundary.

recommendation.title: Define audit and trust boundary first
recommendation.body: Document the threat model, redaction and retention rules, and compatibility plan before changing hook runner behavior or config.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the clearest recent history across the plugin hook runner, hook type surface, and registry contracts that would carry this decision into implementation.
